recent_articles.title: Green energy key to India’s future growth: Naidu - The Hindu

Chandrababu Naidu**, Andhra Pradesh's Chief Minister, emphasized India's need for energy security and sustainable development through green energy and decentralized power systems. recent_articles.title: Will hear Trinamool pleas on victory margins being less than deleted votes in SIR, says Supreme Court - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, leader of the **Trinamool Congress**, appeared before the Supreme Court on Monday, May 11, 2026, to argue that deletions made during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal affected election results. recent_articles.title: Andhra GST officials urged to support tech-driven tax reforms - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Chandrababu Naidu lays foundation for Google’s ₹1.35 lakh crore AI data centre in Visakhapatnam - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: BJD asks Odisha Speaker to disqualify MLAs who cross-voted in Rajya Sabha election - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Blue City a blend of infrastructure and environmental planning - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Veteran politician Nadendla Bhaskara Rao registered maiden victory in 1978, held CM post for a month - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nadendla Bhaskara Rao**, former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, passed away at the age of 90 on April 22, 2026.  He is remembered for his brief tenure as Chief Minister in 1984, which was triggered by a political revolt against **N.T. Rama Rao**. The episode led to landmark constitutional reform and remains a controversial chapter in Indian politics. Bhaskara Rao's legacy includes his role in founding the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and his later association with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).  He is survived by his sons, including Andhra Pradesh Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar.

recent_articles.title: Ex-Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nadendla Bhaskara Rao dies at 90 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nadendla Bhaskara Rao**, a former Chief Minister of undivided Andhra Pradesh and co-founder of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), died at a private hospital in Hyderabad on Wednesday, April 22, 2026. He was 90 years old and had been undergoing treatment for old-age-related ailments. His son, **Nadendla Manohar**, is the Minister for Civil Supplies, Food and Consumer Affairs in the TDP-led NDA government in Andhra Pradesh.  **Bhaskara Rao** played a key role in the formation of the TDP in 1982 and was later expelled from the party. He served as an MLA from various constituencies and also held positions in the Lok Sabha and BJP. His body will be kept at his residence for public viewing before being cremated on April 24th.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Will NDA, under AIADMK, be lucky this time? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **AIADMK**, led by Edappadi K. Palaniswami, is seeking to regain power in Tamil Nadu after two unsuccessful attempts at the polls. Despite internal tensions and controversies surrounding the Delimitation and Women’s Reservation Bills, the AIADMK is hoping to capitalize on public dissatisfaction with the DMK government.
